import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 273
*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/273](https://www.erdosproblems.com/273)
-/

namespace Erdos273

/--
Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are of the form $p-1$ for some primes $p \geq 5$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_273 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ, ∀ i, ∃ (p : ℕ), p.Prime ∧ 5 ≤ p ∧
    c.moduli i = Ideal.span {↑(p - 1)} := by
  sorry

/--
Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are of the form $p-1$ for some primes $p \geq 3$?
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_273.variants.three : answer(True) ↔ ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℕ, ∀ i, ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ 3 ≤ p ∧
    c.moduli i = Ideal.span {↑(p - 1)} := by
  -- TODO(Paul-Lez): find reference for this and perhaps formalize the proof?
  sorry

end Erdos273

reformulations.difference: The source concerns a finite distinct covering of the integers. Lean instead uses StrictCoveringSystem ℕ, whose translates of principal ideals are one-sided progressions a + mℕ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An integer cover gives a natural-number cover by replacing each residue modulo m = p − 1 with its least nonnegative representative r: a natural number is congruent to r exactly when it belongs to r + mℕ. Conversely, for a finite natural-number cover, let M be the product of its positive moduli. For any integer z, the natural number z mod M is covered; since every modulus divides M, the corresponding integer residue class also contains z. Both constructions preserve the moduli and their distinctness: principal ideals generated by natural numbers are equal over either ℕ or ℤ exactly when their generators are equal. The exact existential propositions were proved equivalent for every prime lower bound b ≥ 3 in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean, without using the file's sorry theorems.

review.notes: Both declarations match Erdős–Graham, p. 24. That page explicitly requires finite systems with distinct moduli, asks the p ≥ 5 question, and credits Selfridge with a p = 3 example using divisors of 360; it supplies the reference sought by the variant's TODO. The cited erdosproblems.com page returned a Cloudflare challenge despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so the primary book was used for statement verification. The current community database still records problem 273 as open. Boundary checks and an explicit 12-class witness for the solved variant were verified in Lean; both the witness proof and the ℕ/ℤ equivalence have no sorryAx dependency.
